speaker: Doctor
text: Let me start by asking: How long have you been experiencing these skin lesions, and have they changed in size, color, or shape recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that detailed history; given the non-healing nature of these lesions and your significant smoking history, have you noticed any pain, bleeding, or ulceration in these specific areas? Also, do you recall any similar skin changes in other locations, such as your lips, ears, or soles of your feet?

REQUEST TEST: Complete blood count (CBC) and Comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP) to assess general health before biopsy.

REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide high-resolution dermoscopic images of both the penile and digital lesions to evaluate for asymmetry, border irregularity, and color variegation.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (penile and acral)

Doctor: The previous suggestion of pneumonia seems incorrect given these skin findings; your heavy smoking history combined with non-healing lesions on the penis and finger is highly suspicious for Squamous Cell Carcinoma. We need to proceed immediately with a biopsy of the penile lesion to confirm the diagnosis and determine the extent of the disease.
